title: Maximum Product of Subsequences With an Alternating Sum Equal to K
summary: Given an integer array nums and two integers k and limit, find a non-empty subsequence of nums that has an alternating sum equal to k, maximizes the product of its elements without exceeding limit, and return the product.
statement: Given an integer array nums and two integers k and limit, find a non-empty subsequence of nums that has an alternating sum equal to k, maximizes the product of its elements without exceeding limit, and return the product. If no such subsequence exists, return -1.
constraints: nums has up to 150 values between 0 and 12; limit is 1 to 5,000.
Choose a nonempty subsequence in original order. Its alternating sum is even-position sum minus odd-position sum.
Among subsequences with alternating sum k and product at most limit, return the largest product, or -1 if none exists.
hints: A subsequence state needs its alternating sum, the parity of its chosen length, and its product; all three affect a future choice.
Process values in order and extend a snapshot of existing states so each array position is used at most once.
Start a one-value state, extend every prior state with the parity-selected sign, and retain products with one overflow sentinel so a later zero can still make them legal.
Induction over processed prefixes represents every legal subsequence exactly by its sufficient state, including zero-product choices.
editorial: Induction over processed prefixes represents every legal subsequence exactly by its sufficient state, including zero-product choices.

tests.explanation: The full subsequence has alternating sum 1-2+3=2 and product six.
The pair [3,3] has alternating sum zero and the largest permitted product, nine.
